note: Every field of a compiled program's outputs, and whether the chart adapter carries it. Read by scripts/check-chart-surface.mjs, which compiles a study declaring two of everything, builds a descriptor from it, and refuses a field the program carries that this file does not mention, a field mentioned here that the format no longer has, and a declaration the descriptor drops whose count is not recorded below. A narrowing is a fact about this chart's descriptor and never about the language: the compiled program carries all of it, and another host may draw all of it. Some of what the descriptor carries depends on the chart the host states in ChartAdapterOptions.chartVersion; an entry under refused names the version it is drawn from, and the check builds its fixture's descriptor as a host stating that version would, and proves the refusal below it.

resolution.note: When each member of the descriptor resolves a declaration option that was written as an input(). A declaration option may be an input() (docs/inputs.md), so the value behind it is the host's stored setting rather than the literal in the source. The two halves below are the only two answers there are, and a member in neither is one whose answer to a settings change is whatever it happens to be. Read by scripts/check-chart-surface.mjs, which moves one field of each kind and refuses a descriptor member neither list names.

atBuild.why: Resolved once, against the settings descriptorFor was given, because these members are values rather than calls and there is nowhere later to ask. A host that changes a setting and wants the declared shape to follow builds the descriptor again. That is the honest limit of a declared shape: nothing is dropped, and what a member answers is the settings it was built with.

perCall.why: Resolved again on every call, against the settings handed to that call, because these members are functions and the chart passes its current settings into each one. A settings change reaches them with no rebuild.

unusable.why: What every member above resolves to when the host's stored value is one the engine will refuse: the declared default. The engine's own check decides it, `checkSetting` in src/core/engine/inputs.ts, which is the function the load refuses with, so there is one answer to what a stored value is worth rather than an adapter's and an engine's. The value is not repaired on the way to the engine either: it travels exactly as the host stored it and the run stops with OS6019 naming the key and the bound. The shape is still built, because the settings dialog a reader corrects the value in is built from it, and a study that refuses to describe itself is one whose bad setting cannot be reached. Before this, a stored 99 against an input declared max = 8 went into plots[0].priceFormat.precision as written, and the adapter kept a second idea of an unusable value besides: a stored null read as the declared default while the engine refused the same map, and a stored "7" read as neither and landed on the chart's own fallback. Checked by scripts/check-chart-surface.mjs, which moves one field outside its declared bounds, as a value of another type and as null, and reads both the shape and the run. One kind is narrowed and was before this: a "time" input is stored as a wall clock string and delivered to a script as a timestamp, and the conversion between them is the host's own, which run.ts has and this does not. So a time input written into a declaration option resolves here to the stored string rather than to the number the engine will hold, and a field that wants a number falls back to its own default. The compiler refuses a time input in a string field, OS3011, so the string itself never reaches one.

narrowed.why: The declaration's stable identity. A marker reaches the chart as an event on a bar rather than as a declared row, and the set is rebuilt from the run on every recompute, so there is nothing for an identity to be kept against.

The chart draws a marker's text in the plate's own colour and has no second colour for it. A version 1 compiler writes null into this field for every program, because signal() takes one colour and it is the plate's.

The grid's stable identity. It pairs the declaration with the cell buffer the engine wrote, and it is carried as the grid's id through the list of grids where the host states a chart that has one (see refused below). The single table hook an older chart reads has no id to carry it into, and needs none, because such a chart draws one grid and has nothing to tell apart.

The grid's legend and settings name. The chart's grid is a block of cells pinned to a corner, with no heading and no settings row of its own, so there is nowhere to put it. A host that lists a study's outputs reads it from the program.
The frame slot holding the table handle, which is an engine fact rather than a chart one. The adapter pairs a declaration with its cells by key instead.

The chart evaluates each watched condition once for each bar that is new since it last looked, which is oncePerBar. once would need state that outlives a recompute, and everyUpdate would need the condition judged again on a bar that is still moving; the entry is handed neither.

refused.why: A chart before 2.5.4 has one table hook, so one grid per study reaches the pane. From 2.5.4 the descriptor also has a list of grids, each under a stable id, and every declared grid is drawn through it, in declaration order and under its declaration's key, while the single hook keeps the first. A host that states an earlier chart version, or none, or one that cannot be read, has a study declaring a second grid refused before any bar runs, naming the second grid, rather than drawn with its second panel missing.

A chart before 2.5.4 draws a band in one colour for each side for the whole run. From 2.5.4 the band has a per-bar colour callback, and colorUpChannel and colorDownChannel are carried through it: each bar answers the colour computed for the side the band is on there, decided as the chart decides it, the first plot at or above the second; an absent colour leaves the bar unpainted; a side that is not computed keeps its declared colour; and the band's opacity dims a computed colour exactly as it dims a constant one. A host that states an earlier chart version, or none, or one that cannot be read, has such a band refused before any bar runs rather than drawn in a colour the script did not choose.
